result.rationale: The diff shows the Office365 refreshAccessToken previously used refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse, logged console.error with the zod error and raw MS response, then proceeded to prisma.credential.update regardless (log-and-continue). The replacement calls parseRefreshTokenResponse, which throws a generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' shared across apps (Zoom, Google, Salesforce use the same helper), losing the provider payload and app identifier from logs and escalating a transient parse failure to a hard throw that aborts the refresh. The described mechanism is fully verifiable

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces Office365's per-app error handling: the removed console.error was the only place the zod error and the raw MS response body were logged, the shared throw emits a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" with no app identifier or provider payload, and the failure mode escalates from log-and-continue (proceeding with the still-valid previous token) to a hard throw that aborts the refresh. Production Office365 auth incidents become undiagnosable — the MS response body appears nowhere in logs — and a transient provider anomaly that previously degraded to using the previous token now fails the entire calendar operation for the user; the same generic message is thrown by Zoom, Google and Salesforce, so the logs cannot even name the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, logged `console.error(...)` including the zod error and `responseJson`, then continued (no throw) and still updated the credential with the existing `o365AuthCredentials`. The diff replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and contains no provider/app context or payload logging. This is a diff-verifiable change in failure behavior (from log-and-continue to hard throw) and removes the only logged MS response body, reducing diagnosability; the same generic throw is reused across multiple providers in this PR (e.g., Zoom/Google/Salesforce).
